faults.rationale: Empty scope mapping is no longer replaced by the default bounded synthetic scope. Witness: assess('admission_accounting', {}, scope={}).scope is {} instead of the default.

Default scope is one shared mutable dict, so mutating one verdict's scope leaks into every later default-scope verdict. Witness: v=assess(...); v.scope['kind']='x'; a second assess(...) reports kind 'x'.
Verdict scope aliases the caller's scope mapping, so a later caller mutation changes an already-returned verdict. Witness: s={'a':1}; v=assess(..., scope=s); s['a']=2; v.as_dict()['scope']['a']==2.
as_dict returns the verdict's own scope object instead of a copy; mutating the returned dict mutates the frozen verdict. Witness: d=v.as_dict(); d['scope']['x']=1; 'x' in v.scope.
An empty-string decisive_if is silently dropped from as_dict. Witness: EvidenceVerdict('c', EvidenceStatus.ESTABLISHED, 'r', {}, (), '').as_dict() lacks 'decisive_if'.
EvidenceVerdict is no longer immutable. Witness: setattr(v, 'reason', 'tampered') succeeds instead of raising FrozenInstanceError.
Verdicts lose value equality (and become identity-hashable). Witness: assess(c, o) == assess(c, o) is False.
Status loses StrEnum str()/format semantics while .value and == 'established' still hold. Witness: str(EvidenceStatus.ESTABLISHED) is 'EvidenceStatus.ESTABLISHED'; f'{status}' changes.
Adds a hidden alias member; iteration is unchanged but EvidenceStatus['UNKNOWN'] and __members__ gain an entry. Witness: list(EvidenceStatus.__members__).

missing_evidence on the verdict becomes a list, not the declared tuple (as_dict unchanged). Witness: assess('admission_accounting', {}).missing_evidence == ('accepted execution/effect observation',) is False.
